h1: New Jersey Car Service from NYC

intro: JFK sits inside Queens, so a car from Astoria, Long Island City, Forest Hills, or Flushing is one of the shortest airport runs in the city — but short doesn't mean simple when the Van Wyck backs up. Aria locks a flat $135 sedan / $195 SUV from anywhere in Queens to JFK, so a 20-minute trip never turns into a surge-priced surprise.

sections.h2: Flat Rate From Every Queens Neighborhood
sections.html: Whether you're in Astoria near the Grand Central Parkway or in Jamaica minutes from the AirTrain, the rate is fixed at booking — no metering, no surge during the morning bank at JFK. Because we track your flight, an early departure or a delayed return simply moves the pickup; the price doesn't budge.

The Van Wyck Expressway is the classic JFK chokepoint. Our chauffeurs route by live traffic — Grand Central to the Van Wyck, or surface streets through Kew Gardens when the highway seizes up. Build in a little cushion for morning peak (7–9 a.m.) and Sunday evening returns, and your chauffeur handles the rest.

An Executive Sedan carries up to 3 with luggage; a Premium SUV handles 6 or a golf-bag-and-family load; an Executive Sprinter moves a full crew of up to 14. All include a TLC-licensed chauffeur, bottled water, and luggage assistance.

faqs.q: How much is a car from Queens to JFK?
faqs.a: A flat $135 for a sedan and $195 for an SUV from anywhere in Queens, including tolls and gratuity-free base pricing. Rates hold 24/7 with no surge.

faqs.q: How long does it take from Queens to JFK?
faqs.a: Typically 20–40 minutes depending on your neighborhood and the Van Wyck. Astoria and LIC run longer; Jamaica and Ozone Park are quickest.

faqs.q: Do you track my flight from JFK?
faqs.a: Yes — for JFK pickups we track your flight and adjust automatically, with 60 minutes of complimentary wait time and meet-and-greet at baggage claim.

intro: From White Plains, Scarsdale, Rye, or Bronxville, JFK is a 60–90 minute run down the Hutch and across the Whitestone or Throgs Neck — a drive you don't want to make in your own car and leave parked for a week. Aria runs flat $225 sedan / $295 SUV from Westchester to JFK, tolls included, with a chauffeur who leaves early enough to beat the bridges.

sections.html: Westchester-to-JFK lives or dies on the East River crossings. Our chauffeurs weigh the Whitestone vs. Throgs Neck vs. the RFK in real time, and know when the Cross Bronx is a parking lot to be avoided entirely. For early flights we recommend departing Westchester at least 2.5 hours before wheels-up.

Long-term parking at JFK plus the schlep from the lot — or Metro-North to Grand Central, then the AirTrain with luggage — turns a simple trip into a multi-transfer ordeal. A private car is door-to-terminal with your bags handled, and for HPN-area travelers we also cover Westchester County Airport transfers from $80.
Premium SUVs seat up to 6 with room for a week's luggage; Sprinters handle the full extended family. Complimentary child seats are available on request — just tell us your kids' ages when you book.

faqs.q: How much is a car from Westchester to JFK?
faqs.a: Flat rates are $225 for a sedan and $295 for an SUV, all tolls included, from most of central and southern Westchester. Northern towns may vary slightly — we quote up front.

faqs.q: How early should I leave Westchester for a JFK flight?
faqs.a: We recommend departing at least 2.5 hours before departure for domestic and 3 hours for international, to absorb the Hutch, the bridges, and the Cross Bronx.

faqs.q: Do you also serve Westchester County Airport (HPN)?
faqs.a: Yes — HPN transfers start around $80 locally, and we connect HPN to Manhattan and the other NYC airports as well.

intro: Albany is a 150-mile straight run up the Thruway — comfortable in a private car, miserable on a crowded Amtrak with luggage and a laptop you can't quite open. Aria runs flat-rate chauffeured service from anywhere in NYC to Albany and the Capital Region for $650 sedan / $850 SUV, tolls included, on your schedule rather than the train's.

sections.h2: Why Private Car Beats the Train to Albany
sections.html:
• Door-to-door — no Penn Station scrum, no cab at the far end
  • Leave when you want, not when Amtrak decides
  • Work in privacy with Wi-Fi and space to spread out
  • Flat rate locked at booking — no peak-fare gouging
  • Ideal for legislators, lobbyists, and business travelers on Capitol runs

The trip runs up the Henry Hudson or the FDR to the Thruway (I-87), a clean 2.5–3.5 hours depending on your NYC pickup and traffic north of the city. Your chauffeur handles fuel, tolls, and rest stops; you handle your inbox — or nothing at all.
Many Albany trips are same-day round trips or multi-stop Capital Region itineraries. As-directed hourly service keeps one chauffeur with you for the day; we'll quote the full program up front.

faqs.q: How much is a car from NYC to Albany?
faqs.a: A flat $650 for a sedan and $850 for an SUV, all tolls included, for the roughly 150-mile trip up the Thruway.

faqs.q: How long does the drive to Albany take?
faqs.a: Typically 2.5–3.5 hours depending on your NYC pickup point and traffic. Your chauffeur tracks conditions and plans departure accordingly.

faqs.q: Do you offer round trips to Albany?
faqs.a: Yes — same-day round trips and multi-stop Capital Region itineraries are available on as-directed hourly service. We quote the full program in advance.

h1: NYC to Atlantic City Car Service
intro: Atlantic City is close enough for a day trip and far enough that you don't want to drive it yourself, park in a casino garage, and drive home tired. Aria runs flat-rate chauffeured service from NYC to AC for $525 sedan / $695 SUV — arrive relaxed, leave whenever you're ready, and let someone else handle the Parkway.

sections.h2: The Smart Way to Do AC
sections.html:
• No driving after a long night or a long day at the tables
  • Door-to-casino — Borgata, Ocean, Hard Rock, or the Boardwalk
  • Flat rate both ways; wait-and-return options for day trips
  • Room for a group in an SUV or Sprinter — split the cost, split the fun
  • Chauffeur handles the Garden State Parkway and tolls

The drive runs through the Holland or Lincoln Tunnel to the Turnpike and down the Garden State Parkway — about 125 miles and 2.5–3 hours in normal traffic. Summer weekends to the Shore add time; your chauffeur plans around it.

An Executive Sprinter carries up to 14 for a bachelor party, birthday, or casino outing. For overnight trips we can drop and return, or hold the vehicle as-directed. Tell us the plan and we'll quote it flat.

faqs.q: How much is a car from NYC to Atlantic City?
faqs.a: A flat $525 for a sedan and $695 for an SUV each way, tolls included, for the roughly 125-mile trip down the Parkway. Sprinters available for groups.

faqs.q: Can you wait and bring us back the same day?
faqs.a: Yes — day-trip wait-and-return and overnight options are available on as-directed service. We'll quote the round trip up front.
